messages:
rachel: Quick sync: we need a final decision for SDK telemetry defaults before the SDK release. Topics: default log level, request-id header naming/propagation, OTel integration ergonomics, and default redaction. Thoughts?

tony: my 2c: default log level = WARN for production libs; allow REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL override. In dev mode (NODE_ENV != production or REDWOOD_DEV=true) set INFO.

vik: Agree on WARN. For header names I'm leaning to short `x-rw-request-id` to reduce header length, but we must accept `x-request-id` and `x-amzn-trace-id` and copy them into our header if present. SDK should always emit both headers when it creates a new id to maximize interoperability.

emily: For OTel: SDKs should not force an exporter. Provide an opt-in connector: enable_otel=true + otlp_endpoint. Also expose a hook: onCreateSpan(span, metadata) so customers can decorate spans with app-specific attrs. Auto-add attributes: redwood.model, redwood.request_id, redwood.input_redacted=true/false.

rachel: Good. How about log format? JSON by default with keys: ts, level, msg, module, request_id, trace_id, span_id, latency_ms. Also include an `event` field for structured payloads.

tony: Redaction rules: default safe-set: redact any field named "prompt" or "user_input" in structured events, mask bearer tokens, emails, and cc-like numbers. Instead of dropping prompt we emit prompt_hash: sha256(prompt)[:12]. Important: hash must be deterministic and configurable so teams can reproduce locally. Document how to compute and how to match in logs.

emily: Implementation detail: do redaction at the logger layer and again at OT exporter layer to be safe. Add config option `REDWOOD_REDACTION_LEVEL` with values: none/dev/audit/strict (default strict). strict -> redact prompt text and PII; dev -> keep prompt but mask sensitive patterns.

vik: For request ids: generation algorithm: uuid v4 for randomness. Provide `redwood.request_id()` util in each SDK so apps can reuse same id across internal logs before calling SDK. Also ensure metrics exporter attaches request_id as attribute for counters/timers.

tony: We should also provide a lightweight per-request context helper in each SDK: `withRequestContext({requestId, traceparent}, fn)` that binds logger context and OTel context for the duration of fn. Makes it easier for web frameworks.

emily: On OTel headers, support W3C traceparent/tracestate and legacy `X-Amzn-Trace-Id`. When propagating, prefer W3C if present.

rachel: Audit and safety: if someone enables full prompt logging via REDWOOD_ALLOW_FULL_PROMPTS=true, require a confirmation in the console (docs + audit log event) and block by default on prod accounts.

stakeholder-bot: note saved: telemetry defaults doc draft created at 1718154600

vik: For debugging flow: add `REDWOOD_SDK_TRACE_ID_HEADER` env var to let users override header name. Also log an abbreviated stack on WARN+ errors (module path + fn) but avoid including local file content.

tony: one more: include request_id in error reports to Sentry/Datadog and include a linkable URL `https://console.redwood.ai/logs?request_id=...` for easy triage.

emily: Action items: I'll add the OT hook API sketch to the node/python SDK readme.

rachel: I'll update the DX page with env var table and an example of computing prompt hash and redaction levels. Target: RFC by EOD Friday. Any objections?

emily: none from me.

vik: none.
